_comment: Retrieval eval baseline (#37 -> hard gate, #139). Per-mode mean metrics over the golden corpus. This is a HARD GATE, not reporting-only: the compose retrieval eval fails the build when any per-mode metric regresses beyond EVAL_GATE_TOLERANCE below these numbers (tests/evals/eval_gate.py), on top of the absolute RETRIEVAL_MIN_RECALL5 floor. A green run on main ratchets these values up to max(current, baseline) per mode/metric (never down) and opens a PR with the ratchet + a trend-history line (.github/workflows/integration.yml) -- branch protection on main blocks github-actions[bot] from pushing directly, so the ratchet lands as a PR instead of a push. RE-SEEDED 2026-08-12 (#237): this is a DOWNWARD move on keyword.mrr, which the automated ratchet cannot make by construction, so it lands as a reviewed baseline edit. ADR 0004's 2026-08-06 amendment deliberately left the baseline at flag-OFF numbers so CI would judge the flag-ON default (#146, per-document diversification) together with #129 (format-aware chunking) on its own merits. CI returned that verdict on main sha edd9f0c and again on the 2026-08-11 nightly, bit-identical both times: 8 of 9 gated metrics flat or improved (recall@5 +0.038 semantic/hybrid and +0.077 keyword, nDCG@5 up in all three modes, multi_doc_crowding recall 0.5 -> 1.0), and ONE regressed -- keyword.mrr 0.8205 -> 0.7821. That delta is exactly 0.5/13, i.e. a single golden query in the 'general' category whose judged-relevant document moved from rank 1 to rank 2 in keyword mode; every other category scores mrr 1.0 in all three modes. Accepting one rank-position slip on one query in exchange for corpus-wide recall and nDCG gains is the trade ADR 0004 was approved to make, so these flag-ON numbers become the baseline. FIXED 2026-08-12 (#236): the gate's tolerance is now DERIVED from corpus resolution instead of fixed at EVAL_GATE_TOLERANCE. EVAL_GATE_TOLERANCE (default 0.02) is a floor; the effective per-metric tolerance is max(EVAL_GATE_TOLERANCE, min_detectable_delta(metric, n)), where n is the number of gated queries (category != 'abstention', currently 13) and min_detectable_delta is the smallest possible single-query move for that metric family (0.5/n for mrr, 1/n for recall@k, (1 - 1/log2(3))/n for ndcg@k) -- see tests/evals/eval_gate.py (min_detectable_delta, effective_tolerance), docs/testing.md, and this ADR's amendment (docs/adr/0003-traffic-mined-retrieval-evals.md). This baseline's VALUES are unchanged by that fix -- only the tolerance the gate compares them with changed -- so a future single rank slip within min_detectable_delta no longer requires another manual re-seed.
